claims.excerpt: How GRACE Follow-On Uses Satellite Separation to Investigate Water Movement
claims.claim: GRACE Follow-On uses satellite separation measurements to investigate water movement.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass. The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets and changes in sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.narrative: Explain how GRACE Follow-On’s two satellites use changes in the distance between them to help investigate water movement on Earth.
claims.explanation: The title accurately summarizes the measurement-to-inference purpose described in the source.
claims.materiality: Central framing; faithful to the source.

claims.excerpt: As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first
claims.claim: During passage by a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite before the trailing satellite.
claims.label: F1 minor immaterial imprecision
claims.evidence: As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing one.
claims.narrative: As the pair passes a larger mass concentration, gravity acts on the leading satellite first
claims.explanation: The source locates the described effect as the pair approaches the mass concentration; “as they pass” is less precise and may suggest a different point in the encounter. The narrative also uses “passes” in its selected-story summary, though its progression and the source say “approaches.”
claims.materiality: Minor timing imprecision; the leading satellite being affected first is supported.

claims.materiality: Central to the described separation-change mechanism; accurate.
